sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 WebGPURenderer and TSL; Rapier 2D 0.19.3; Gamepad API; Web Audio; PeerJS 1.5.5; AI Hub Session Protocol v1 / client 1.4.0
sourceInformation.artDirection: Stylized cel shading, navy ink outlines, warm paper, coral / teal print palette
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer and AnimationClip for brick destruction; procedural trails, particles and paddle squash
sourceInformation.audio: Code-generated synth music (10% default), effects and Animalese-style gibberish voices; no audio files
sourceInformation.online: 1–2 player shared-world co-op, AI Hub sessions, standalone WebRTC rooms and same-device BroadcastChannel
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium with software WebGPU; 26 checks covering a full scripted campaign, keyboard, emulated standard gamepads, touch, offline file delivery, Web Audio waveforms, two-page networking and five official AI Hub scenarios. Screenshots checked through the WebGL2 fallback.
sourceInformation.research: none; supplied AI Hub integration specification read directly

testingFeedback: Automated tests caught 2 game defects. Additional controller, shared-world rendering and lobby lifecycle findings from review were also fixed.
1 critical issue: the ball could become trapped between the DOUBLE stage paddles. Fixed with sensor colliders and descending-only paddle rebounds.
The natural AI full-campaign playthrough exposed the DOUBLE-stage trap and then verified all four stages reach victory.
Version-string checks confirmed packaging but provided little gameplay coverage.
engineFeedback: Three.js TSL made the cel-shaded palette easy to control, and AnimationMixer clips gave brick destruction a consistent pop.
Ordinary solid paddle collisions trapped ascending balls under the extra paddle. Headless WebGPU screenshots were blank, so screenshots used the WebGL2 fallback while state tests verified WebGPU.
Paddle rebound rules, campaign and UI state machines, controller focus, procedural audio and authoritative shared-world snapshots.
Coordinating fast-ball physics, asynchronous GPU rendering and multiplayer state in a single-file game.
none; only public engine APIs were used.
A built-in cel material and outline pass that behave consistently across WebGPU and WebGL2.
promptFeedback: The named arcade source, complete-demo scope and controller-first TV focus made the design direction clear.
No internet research was requested alongside linked online integration instructions. Only the supplied integration specification and required dependencies were fetched.
Delivering a polished four-stage game with offline single-file playback, every input method and both standalone and Hub co-op.
Include a versioned Hub contract inline and state whether standalone online play should use a public signaling service.

aiHub.name: Super Bounceout
aiHub.description: An ink-and-paper brick breaker with four handcrafted stages, captive multiballs, double paddles and a wall that won’t sit still. Make a clean break solo or share the paddle work in local and online co-op.
aiHub.controls: Move: left stick / D-pad, mouse or A/D / arrows; serve: Cross / A / Space / tap; ink burst: Triangle / Y / Shift / right click; pause: Options / Esc.
